paper.title: Thompson Sampling for 1-Dimensional Exponential Family Bandits

unmapped: 1-dimensional canonical exponential family with general sufficient statistic T(x) (covers e.g. Pareto and Weibull, heavy-tailed); F twice differentiable with continuous second derivative
settings.definition_quote: An \emph{exponential family $K$-armed bandit} is a $K$-armed bandit for which the reward distributions $p_a$ are known to be elements of an exponential family of distributions $\cP(\Theta)$.

conditions: rewards from a 1-dimensional canonical exponential family

source.label: eq:as-opt
source.quote: Suppose that the rewards distributions belong to a $1$-dimensional canonical exponential family and that $\pi_J$ is the Jeffrey's prior. Then, \lim_{T\ra \infty} \frac {\cR(\phi^{TS,\pi_J},T)}{\ln T} = \sum_{a = 1}^K \frac{\mu(\theta_{a^*})-\mu(\theta_a)}{\K(\theta_a, \theta_{a^*})}

results.notes: Stated as a limit equality (matches Lai-Robbins); recorded as limsup upper bound. Follows from Theorem 2 which assumes a unique optimal arm. Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret.

symbols.C_eps_P: unspecified problem-dependent constant C(epsilon, P) depending on epsilon and the problem

conditions: unique optimal arm: mu_1 > mu_a for all a != 1
rewards from a 1-dimensional canonical exponential family

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: Assume that $\mu_1>\mu_a$ for all $a\neq 1$, and that $\pi_{a,0}$ is taken to be the Jeffrey's prior over $\Theta$. Then for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists a constant $\cC(\epsilon,\cP)$ depending on $\epsilon$ and on the problem $\mathcal{P}$ such that the regret of Thompson Sampling using the Jeffrey's prior satisfies \cR(\phi^{TS,\pi_J},T) \leq \frac{1+\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\left(\sum_{a=2}^{K}\frac{(\mu_1-\mu_a)}{\K(\theta_a,\theta_1)}\right)\ln(T) + \mathcal{C}(\epsilon,\mathcal{P}).

results.notes: eps is a free analysis parameter, holds for every eps>0 (eps<1 implicitly). Constant not explicit.
